chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Finding Lena Horne for Charlie Barnet at the Valencia and Paramount
summary: Horace tracks Lena Horne down at Harlem's Regent Theatre and brings her to the Bronx to sing with Barnet; she buys a gown, breaks it up, and goes on to the Paramount. Barnet bets on horses, and Horace later toured with Lena.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: MR. HENDERSON: Lena Horne. She had just come in from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania having been divorced from her husband, so there's a little theatre in New York City -- there was, I don't know if there is now or not -- called the Regent at 116th and Seventh Avenue. So I went back stage in the Apollo Theatre, and they told me that Lena Horne had just left there, but she was going to this particular theatre, the Regent. So I immediately went to the Regent, and I had her paged, and I got her, and I talked with her, and I wouldn't tell her what I wanted, but we got in the car, and I asked her was she available to sing. And we talked and everything, and she said, "Yeah." "Well I won't tell you. I've got a surprise for you." So we rode on up to the Bronx, and we got almost to the Valencia Theatre, and out on the marquee was Charlie Barnet and his band. So she says, "What is this?" And I began to tell her what's happening. So I introduced her to Charlie, and

Charlie told her what was happening. They went downstairs, and rehearsed, and she said, 'Well I don't have any gowns, or anything.' She said, 'I just came to New York to visit,' so he gave her some money to go out and get a gown, and she went in the next show. And broke it up of course, and we rehearsed a couple of things downstairs, like 'The Captain and His Men,' and some other great things. She ad libbed a few things. So to make a long story short, we were set for the Paramount Theatre. So we went to the Paramount Theatre, and Lena Horne was his vocalist there, and we broke it up. And a funny thing about Charlie. This -- I've got to inject this.

Charlie always liked to play the horses. He had a wire on the back stage to the race track, and he won, and came across the stage and threw hundred dollar bills at the guys, and all this kind of stuff. He was quite a guy. He was funny, you know, and anyway, Lena went on and broke it up there, and of course, the scouts saw her and she went to Hollywood to the Trocadero out there. I don't need to say anything else about it, except I later joined her as her pianist and arranger and we toured all over the RKO theatres, all over the United States. I had a lovely time with her. She's quite a girl. We played a lot of the army camps, and we lived in a plane, man. That's the only thing I didn't like. My stomach couldn't take it, you know. We even went to Camp Joseph Robinson in Little Rock, Arkansas, and jumped from
there to Fort Dix, and all these places, all in a day. You know, we played sometimes -- it was a great experience for me. So this is what Charley Barnet did for me.
